NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_terms¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_terms(const Note& other) const

Shared Content Words Between Two Notes¶

intersect_terms(other) is intersect_tokens restricted to content words: it reduces each cell to the set of significant words and returns the ones present in both cells as a TokenBatch. Use it when function words (the, and, with) and short fillers would only add noise to the comparison. The scoring members for the same set are jaccard_terms and overlap_terms.

How the set is built¶

Each cell is tokenized with the ASCII word tokenizer and every token is lowercased. A token joins the set only if it is

  • 4 or more characters long, and

  • not a stopword — the short closed-class list a, an, and, are, as, at, be, by, for, from, in, into, is, it, its, of, on, or, that, the, their, this, to, with.

The set is then deduplicated and case-folded. No stemming is applied, so process and processes are different members.

What is emitted¶

For each cell pair, the members in both sets are emitted in the order they first appear in self, once each; a cell with no shared term contributes an empty range. The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Bytes-mode input raises NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_terms requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs); a numel mismatch raises NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_terms expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: Fillers And Short Words Drop Out¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"The cat sat on the warm mat"})
                       .nlp().intersect_terms(pluss::make_note({"a warm mat and a cat"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["warm"]
offsets: [0, 1]

cat, sat, and mat are only three characters, so they never enter either set; the, on, a, and and are stopwords. warm is the one term the two cells share.

See Also¶

  • NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_tokens: the same operation with no content filter.

  • NoteNlpAccessor::jaccard_terms / NoteNlpAccessor::overlap_terms: score the shared-term overlap.

  • NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_acronyms / NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_citations / NoteNlpAccessor::intersect_symbols: other set kinds.
